law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985
what: The court decides whether an article or thing seized is liable to confiscation under sections 60, 61, or 62 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985, and may order confiscation if it decides so.

1.title: Short title, ext ent and commencement
1.what: This Act is called the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985. It applies to all citizens of India outside India and persons on ships and aircrafts registered in India, wherever they may be. The Act will come into force on a date determined by the Central Government.

2.title: Definitions
2.what: Definitions explained in clear language. Definitions include addict, Board, cannabis (hemp), commercial quantity, controlled delivery, corresponding law, controlled substance, conveyance, essential narcotic drug, illicit traffic, International Convention, manufacture, manufactured drug, medicinal cannabis, Narcotics Commissioner, narcotic drug, opium, opium derivative, opium poppy, poppy straw, poppy straw concentrate, preparation, prescribed, production, Psychotropic substance, small quantity, to import inter-State, to import into India, to export from India, to export inter-State, to transport, use

3.title: Power to add to or omit from the list of psychotr opic substances
3.what: The Central Government can add or remove substances from the list of psychotropic substances based on new information and international agreements.

4.title: Central Government to take measures for preventing and combating abuse of and illicit
4.what: The Central Government shall take measures to prevent and combat abuse of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, including coordination with other authorities, international obligations, assistance to foreign countries, identification and treatment of addicts, and prevention of illicit traffic.

5.title: Officers of Central Government
5.what: The Central Government appoints a Narcotics Commissioner and other officers to exercise powers and perform functions related to the cultivation and production of opium, with oversight from the Central Government or designated authorities.

6.title: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropie Sub stances Consultative Committee
6.what: The Central Government can create an advisory committee, called

7.title: Officers of State Government
7.what: The State Government may appoint officers with such designations as it thinks fit for the purposes of this Act.

7A.title: National Fund for Control of Drug Abuse
7A.what: The Central Government can establish a National Fund for Control of Drug Abuse, which is used for various measures related to drug abuse, such as combating trafficking, controlling abuse, identifying and rehabilitating addicts, preventing drug abuse, educating the public, and supplying drugs to addicts where necessary.

7B.title: Annual report of activities financed under the Fund
7B.what: The Central Government must publish an annual report in the Official Gazette, detailing activities financed under section 7A and statements of accounts.

8.title: Prohibition of certain operations
8.what: No person shall cultivate any coca plant or gather any portion of a coca plant; cultivate the opium poppy or any cannabis plant; produce, manufacture, possess, sell, purchase, transport, warehouse, use, consume, import inter-State, export inter-State, import into India, export from India or tranship any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance, except for medical or scientific purposes and in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

8A.title: Prohibition of certain activities relating to property derived from offence
8A.what: No person shall convert, transfer, conceal, disguise, acquire, possess, or use property derived from an offence for any illegal purpose.

9.title: Power of Central Government to permit, control and regulate
9.what: The Central Government may permit and regulate various activities related to narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances, including cultivation, production, possession, sale, purchase, transport, import, export, use, and consumption. The government can also prescribe rules for licenses, permits, and fees for these activities. The power includes the ability to fix limits on licenses, require cultivators to deliver opium to authorized officers, weigh and classify opium, and provide compensation to cultivators. Additionally, the government has the authority to regulate manufacturing, importation, exportation, and transhipment of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances.

9A.title: Power to control and reg ulate controlled substances
9A.what: The Central Government can regulate or prohibit the production, manufacture, supply, and distribution of controlled substances if it's in the public interest.

10.title: Power of State Government to permit, control and regulate
10.what: The State Government has the power to permit, control and regulate the possession, transport, import, export, warehousing, sale, purchase, consumption and use of various substances, including poppy straw, opium, cannabis, medicinal opium, manufactured drugs, and coca leaf. The rules can prescribe additional requirements for effective control, such as declaring places for warehousing, regulating safe custody, levying fees, and issuing licenses for cultivation and trade. The State Government also has the authority to fix limits on licences for cannabis cultivation, require cultivators to deliver produce to authorized officers, and set prices for cannabis delivered. The rules can also specify forms and conditions for licenses or permits and the authorities by which they may be granted.

11.title: Narcotic drugs and psychotropic substanc es, etc., not liable to distress o r attachment
11.what: No narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, or cannabis plants can be distrained or attached for debt recovery.

12.title: Restrictions over external dealings in narcotic dr ugs and psychotropic substances
12.what: No person can engage in or control a trade where a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance is bought or sold outside India, unless they get permission from the Central Government first.

13.title: Special provisions relating to coca plant and coca leaves for use in the preparation of
13.what: The Central Government may permit the cultivation of coca plants, gathering of their portions, production, possession, sale, purchase, transport, import, export, or importing coca leaves for flavouring agents without alkaloids.

14.title: Special provision relating to cannabis
14.what: The government can allow the cultivation of cannabis plants for industrial purposes (e.g. fibre) or horticultural purposes, subject to certain conditions and as specified in an order.

15.title: Punishment for contraventi on in relation to poppy straw
15.what: Whoever produces, possesses, transports, imports inter-State, exports inter-State, sells, purchases, uses or omits to warehouse poppy straw without permission shall be punishable with imprisonment for 1-20 years and/or fine of up to ₹2 lakh. The court may impose a higher fine.

16.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to coca plant and coca leaves
16.what: Whoever cultivates, gathers, produces, possesses, sells, purchases, transports, imports or uses coca plant or coca leaves without permission will be punished with up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to ₹1 lakh. (₹1 lakh = ₹100,000)

17.title: Punishment for contraventio n in relation to prepared opium
17.what: If you manufacture, possess, sell, purchase, transport, import, export or use prepared opium without following the rules, you can face punishment. The amount of punishment will depend on the quantity involved: if it's small, you might get a fine up to 10,000 rupees or jail time up to one year. If it's slightly more, you could get up to 10 years in jail and a fine up to 1 lakh rupees. For larger quantities, you'll likely face at least 10 years in jail and a fine of at least 1 lakh rupees, but potentially up to 2 lakh rupees.

18.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to opium poppy an d opium
18.what: Whoever cultivates, produces, possesses, sells, purchases, transports, imports inter-State, exports inter-State or uses opium in contravention of any provision of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 20 years or fine up to ₹2 lakhs.

19.title: Punishment for embez zlement of opium by cultivator
19.what: A licensed opium poppy cultivator who misuses or illegally disposes of opium must face a prison sentence of at least 10 years and up to 20 years, along with a fine of at least 1 lakh rupees (up to 2 lakh rupees), unless the court decides otherwise.

20.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to cannabis plant and cannabis
20.what: Whoever cultivates or produces cannabis can be punished with rigorous imprisonment for up to 10 years and/or a fine of up to one lakh rupees.

21.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to manu factured drugs and preparations
21.what: Whoever manufactures, possesses, sells, purchases, transports, imports inter-State, exports inter-State or uses any manufactured drug or preparation containing any manufactured drug shall be punishable with: - up to 1 year imprisonment or/and up to 10,000 rupees fine for small quantity contravention. Up to 7 years imprisonment and up to 1 lakh rupees fine for quantity between small and commercial. Commercial quantity contravention punishable with at least 10 years imprisonment and minimum 1 lakh rupees fine.

22.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to psychotropic substan ces
22.what: A person who breaks any rule about psychotropic substances can be punished with imprisonment (up to 20 years) or/and a fine (up to ₹2 lakhs).

23.title: P unishment for ill egal import in to India, export from India or transhipment of narcotic
23.what: Any person who imports or exports narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances without permission or in violation of this Act will face punishment including imprisonment and/or fines.

24.title: Punishment for external dealings in narcot ic drugs and psychotropic substances in
24.what: Person who engages in or controls trade of obtaining and supplying narcotic drugs/psychotropic substances outside India without permission, shall face imprisonment (minimum 10 years) and/or fine ( minimum ₹1 lakh, maximum ₹2 lakh).

25.title: Punishment for allowing premises, etc., to be used for commission of an offence
25.what: A person who owns or uses a property and allows it to be used for committing an offence can be punished with the same punishment as the committed offence.

25A.title: Punishment for contravention o f orders made under section 9A
25A.what: A person who violates an order under section 9A can be punished with up to 10 years in prison and fined up to ₹1,00,000 (or more).

26.title: Punishment for certain acts by licensee or his servants
26.what: if the holder of any license, permit or authorization granted under this Act omits to maintain accounts or submit returns without reasonable cause, fails to produce license on demand, keeps false accounts, wilfully breaks licensing conditions and faces punishment including imprisonment for up to three years or fine.

27.title: Punishment for consumption of any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance
27.what: The punishment for consuming narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances includes: cocaine/morphine/diacetyl-morphine: up to 1 year imprisonment or Rs 20,000 fine; other substances: up to 6 months imprisonment or Rs 10,000 fine

27A.title: Punishment for financing illicit tr affic and harbouring offenders
27A.what: Whoever indulges in financing or harbouring illicit drug and psychotropic substance trafficking shall face imprisonment for at least 10 years and up to 20 years, along with fines of at least ₹1 lakh (₹20 lakh) and up to ₹2 lakh (up to ₹40 lakh).

27B.title: Punishment for contravention of section 8A
27B.what: Person who contravens section 8A shall get imprisonment of minimum 3 yrs up to 10 yrs and also pay a fine.

28.title: Punishment f or attempts to commit offences
28.what: Attempted offense is punished as if it were successful

29.title: Punishment for ab etment and criminal conspiracy
29.what: Punishment for abetment and criminal conspiracy: Whoever abets or is part of a crime with intent to commit an offence punishable under this Chapter shall be punished with the punishment for that offence, regardless of whether the offence is committed or not.

30.title: Preparation
30.what: If someone makes preparations for an offence or fails to do something which would constitute an offence, they can still be punished if circumstances prevented them from committing the crime.

31.title: Enhanced punishment for offences after previous conviction
31.what: If you have been convicted before of committing or attempting to commit any offence under this Act, you will get a harsher punishment for each subsequent offence: the punishment can be up to 3 times longer imprisonment and twice as much fine as the original punishment.

31A.title: Death penalty for certain offences after previous convi ction
31A.what: Complete explanation: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 31, if any person who has been convicted of the commission of, or attempt to commit, or abetment of, or criminal conspiracy to commit, any of the offences punishable under sections 19, 24, 27A, and for offences involving commercial quantity of any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance, is subsequently convicted of the commission of, or attempt to commit, or abetment of, or criminal conspiracy to commit, an offence relating to engaging in the production, manufacture, possession, transportation, import into India, export from India, or transit, of the narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances specified under 1. The punishment shall not be less than the punishment specified in section 31 or with death.

32.title: Punishment for offence for w hich no punishment is provided
32.what: Offenders who contravene the Act without specified punishment will face imprisonment for up to 6 months, or a fine, or both.

32A.title: No suspension, remission or commutation in any sentence awarded under this Act
32A.what: No sentences awarded under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act can be suspended, remitted, or commuted.

32B.title: Factors to be taken into account for imposing highe r than the minimum punishment
32B.what: The court may consider additional factors when imposing a punishment higher than the minimum, including: use or threat of violence, public office misuse, impact on minors, educational institution involvement, organized crime links, and related illegal activities.

33.title: Application of section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and of the Probation of
33.what: Nothing contained in section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or in the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (20 of 1958) applies to a person convicted under this Act unless they are under 18 years old or the offence is punishable under sections 26 or 27.

34.title: Security for abstaining from commission of offence
34.what: A person convicted of a crime may be ordered to sign a bond promising not to commit future offenses.

35.title: Presumption of culpable mental state
35.what: The court will presume the accused had a culpable mental state unless the accused proves otherwise.

36.title: Constitution of Speci al Court
36.what: A government may create special courts to try narcotics-related cases quickly by notifying the creation in the official gazette.

36A.title: Offences triable by Special Courts
36A.what:
Offences triable by Special Courts

All offences under this Act punishable with imprisonment for a term of more than three years shall be triable only by the Special Court constituted for the area in which the offence has been committed.

Where a person accused of or suspected of commission of an offence under this Act is forwarded to a Magistrate, such Magistrate may authorise detention of such person in custody for a period not exceeding 15 days where it is a Judicial Magistrate and 7 days where it is an Executive Magistrate.

A Special Court may exercise power of a Magistrate having jurisdiction to try a case in relation to an accused person who has been forwarded to it under section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

A Special Court may take cognizance of an offence without the accused being committed to it for trial upon perusal of police report or complaint made by an officer of the Central Government or a State Government authorised in his behalf.

When trying an offence under this Act, a Special Court may try an offence other than an offence under this Act with which the accused may be charged at the same trial.

The High Court may exercise special powers regarding bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, including power to grant bail in cases involving Special Courts.

In respect of persons accused of certain offences, references to 'ninety days' shall be construed as reference to 'one hundred and eighty days', but a Special Court may extend the period up to one year upon report from the Public Prosecutor.

Offences punishable with imprisonment for a term of not more than three years may be tried summarily.

36B.title: Appeal and revision
36B.what: The High Court can exercise all powers listed in Chapters XXIX and XXX of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, as if it was a Court of Session.

36C.title: Application of Code to proc eedings before a Special Court
36C.what: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 applies to proceedings before a Special Court, with the court being treated as a Court of Session and the prosecutor being a Public Prosecutor.

36D.title: Transitional provisions
36D.what: Any offence committed under this Act on or after the commencement of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Act, 1988, shall be tried in a Court of Session instead of a Special Court.

37.title: Offences to be cognizable and non -bailable
37.what: Offences punishable under this Act shall be cognizable and no person accused can be released on bail unless: the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity to oppose the application, and the court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing the person is not guilty and will not commit any offence while on bail.

38.title: Offences by companies
38.what: Every person responsible for a company's business and the company itself can be held guilty of an offence committed by the company, if the person was in charge at the time. The guilt is only waived if the person proves they didn't know about the offence or took all necessary precautions to prevent it.

39.title: Power of court to release certain offenders on probation
39.what: When an addict is found guilty of an offence related to a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance, the court can release them for medical treatment instead of imprisonment if they agree. The court will then monitor their progress and ensure they don't commit any further offences during a specified period (not exceeding 1 year). If they comply, they may be released; otherwise, they'll face punishment upon completion of the period.

40.title: Power of court to publish names, place of business, etc., of certain offenders
40.what: A court can publish certain offender's name, place of business, etc., after they are convicted, but only after the appeal period has expired or been disposed of.

41.title: Power to issue warrant and authorisation
41.what: Power to issue warrant and authorisation for arrest, search, seizure, or forfeiture of property related to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

42.title: Power of entry, search, seizure and arrest without warrant or authorisation
42.what: Officer can enter, search, seize, and arrest without warrant if they have reason to believe an offence has been committed. They can do this between sunrise and sunset, but only if it's not possible to get a warrant or authorisation without giving the person time to hide evidence.

43.title: Power of seizure and arrest in public place
43.what: An officer can seize and arrest someone in a public place if they believe an offence under the Act has been committed, and they have reason to believe that the person is holding illegal substances or property related to them.

44.title: Power of entry, search, seizure and arrest in offences relating to coca plant, opium poppy
44.what: Power of entry, search, seizure and arrest for offences relating to coca plant, opium poppy and cannabis plant. The provisions of sections 41, 42 and 43 apply with some modifications to these specific plants.

45.title: Procedure where seizure of goods liable t o confiscation not pra cticable
45.what: If it's not possible to seize goods that can be confiscated, an authorized officer can tell the owner or person in possession of the goods not to touch, sell, or deal with them without permission from the officer first.

46.title: Duty of land holder to give information of illeg al cultivation
46.what: Holder of land must inform police or department about illegal opium poppy, cannabis, or coca cultivation on their land.

47.title: Duty of certain officers to give info rmation of illegal cultivation
47.what: Officers must report illegal land cultivation of opium poppies, cannabis, or coca plants to police or government departments.

48.title: Power of attachmen t of crop illegally cultivated
48.what: A magistrate can order the attachment of illegal crops like opium poppy, cannabis or coca plant with or without destroying them.

49.title: Power to stop and search conveyance
49.what: If an officer suspects that an animal or conveyance is being used to transport a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance, they can stop the animal or conveyance and rummage through it to search for any contraband.

50.title: Conditions under which search of persons shall be conducted
50.what: If the person to be searched requires it, they must be taken without unnecessary delay to the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate. If a search is made under section 41 or 43, and a female wants to avoid being searched by someone of the same gender, she can request to be searched by a male officer.

50A.title: Power to under take controlled delivery
50A.what: The Director General of Narcotics Control Bureau or an authorised officer can undertake controlled delivery of a consignment to any destination in India or a foreign country with the consent of the relevant authority.

51.title: Provisions of the code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to apply to warrants, arrests, searches
51.what: Provisions of the code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 apply to warrants, arrests, searches and seizures under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985

52.title: Disposal of perso ns arrested and articles seized
52.what: A person arrested and articles seized must be taken to a magistrate or police officer without delay, where they will be disposed of according to law.

52A.title: Disposal of seized narcotic dru gs and psychotropic substances
52A.what: The Central Government may specify narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, controlled substances, or conveyances to be disposed of by an officer after seizure, following a notification in the Official Gazette.

53.title: Power to invest officers of certain departments with powers of an officer -in-charge of a
53.what: The Central Government and State Government can invest certain officers with powers similar to those held by an in-charge of a police station, allowing them to investigate crimes under this Act.

53A.title: Relevancy of statemen ts under certain c ircumstances
53A.what: In certain circumstances, statements made by individuals under investigation may be considered relevant evidence in a prosecution.

54.title: Presumption from possession of illicit articles
54.what: In trials under this Act, it may be presumed that the accused has committed an offence if they are found with articles related to the manufacture of illicit substances, unless otherwise proven.

55.title: Police to take charge of articles seized and delivered
55.what: An officer-in-charge of a police station must keep all seized narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances in safe custody until a Magistrate gives orders, and allow authorized officers to inspect them.

56.title: Obligation of officers to assist each other
56.what: Officers of various departments must help each other when implementing the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act

57.title: Report of arrest and seizure
57.what: Whenever any person arrests or seizes narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances under this Act, they must give a detailed report of the arrest and seizure within 48 hours to their immediate superior officer.

57A.title: Report of seizure of property of the person arrested by the notified officer
57A.what: Report of seizure of property of the person arrested by the notified officer. The officer must submit a report to the correct authority within 90 days after an arrest or seizure, if certain provisions apply.

58.title: Punishment for vexatious entry, search, seizure or arrest
58.what: Any person empowered under sections 42, 43, or 44 who enters/builds searches or causes another to do so without reasonable suspicion, seizures property falsely, detains/surveys/ars arrest maliciously and with false information, can be imprisoned for up to 6 months or fined up to ₹1,000.

59.what: Officer who fails to perform their duties, withdraws themselves from duty, or aids in contravention of Act provisions, will face imprisonment up to 1 year, fine, or both, unless they obtain permission from official superior.

60.what: Liability for confiscation applies to: anything related to an offence under this Act, including drugs, substances, plants, articles, and vehicles, as well as any objects used in or with them, except if the owner proves they were not involved.

61.what: Goods used for concealing any narcotic drug, psychotropic substance or controlled substance used by the person for which goods are liable to confiscation under this Act.

62.what: Sale proceeds of illicit drugs or substances sold by someone who knows they are illegal are also subject to confiscation.

64.what: The Central Government or State Government can offer immunity from prosecution if a person provides full disclosure about a violation of the Act in exchange for immunity.

64A.what: An addict who volunteers to get medical treatment for addiction and completes it is not liable for prosecution related to small amounts of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances.

66.title: Presumption as to documents in certain cases
66.what: The court shall presume that a document is authentic, in the handwriting of a particular person, or was executed by a certain person, unless proven otherwise; admit the document as evidence if it's admissible despite being unstamped; and examine witnesses familiar with the facts to verify its contents.

67.what: Any authorized officer can request information, documents, or personal examination during an investigation under this Act to determine if a law has been broken.

68.what: No officer can reveal how they obtained information about an offense committed.

68A.what: The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to persons who have been convicted of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term of 3[ten] years or more, or to persons who have been convicted of a similar offence by a competent court outside India.

68B.title: Definitions
68B.what: Definitions - In this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires,— (a) “Appellate Tribunal” means the Appellate Tribunal referred to in section 68N; (b) “associate” in relation to a person whose property is liable to be forfei ted under this Chapter, means— (i) any individual who had been or is residing in the resi dential premises (including out-houses) of such person; (ii) any individual who had been or is managing the affairs or keepi ng the accounts of such person; (iii) any association of pers ons, body of individuals, part nership firm, or private company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956), of which such person had been or is a member, partner or director; (iv) any individual who had been or is a member, partner or director of an association of persons, body of individuals, partnership firm or private company referred to in sub-clause (iii) at any time when such person had been or is a member, partner or director of such association, body, partnership firm or private company; (v) any person, who had been or is managing the affairs, or keeping the accounts, of any association of persons, body of individuals, partnership firm or private company r eferred to in sub-clause (iii); (vi) the trustee of any trust, where,— (1) the trust has been created by such person; or (2) the value of the assets contributed by such person (including the value of the assets, if any, contributed by him earlier) to the trust amo unts, on the date on which con tribution is made, to not less than twenty per cent. of the value of the assets of the trust on that date; (vii) where the competent aut hority, for reasons to be reco rded in writing, considers that any properties of such person are held on his behalf by any other person, such other person; (c) “competent authority ” means a n officer of the Central Gover nment auth orised by it under section 68D; (d) “concealment” means the concealment or disguise of the nature, source, disposition, movement or ownership of property and includes the movement or conversion of such property by electronic transmission or by any other means; (e) “freezing” means temporarily prohibiting the transfer, conversion, disposition or movement of property by an order issued under section 68F; (f) “identifying” includes establishment of proof that the pr operty was derived from, o r used in, the illicit traffic; (g) “illegally acquired proper ty”, in relation to any person to whom this Chapter applies, means, — (i) any property acquired by such person, whether before or after the commencement of this Chapter, wholly or partly out of or by means of any inc ome, earnings or assets derived or obtained from or attr ibutable to 2[the contravention of any provisions 3[of this Act or the equivalent value of such property; 68H.what: A notice is sent to a person with known sources of income, earnings or assets if there's reason to believe that some of their properties were acquired illegally. The person must respond within 30 days with information about how they acquired the property. If they don't appear or show cause, the competent authority may record a finding and declare the property forfeited to the Central Government.

68J.what: The person affected must prove that the property is not illegally acquired.

68K.title: Fine in lieu of forfeiture
68K.what: If a person's illegal drug or substance-related property is partially owned, they can pay a fine equal to its market value instead of having it seized. The person must be given a chance to explain their case before being ordered to pay the fine. If they pay the fine within the allowed time frame, their property will be released from seizure.
68K.chapter: Chapter VA apply to any person involved in the case of such arrest or seizure, the officer shall make a

68L.title: Procedure in relation to certain trust properties
68L.what: In cases where a person referred to in sub-clause (vi) of clause (b) of section 68B holds trust properties, the competent authority can serve a notice on the author or contributor of the trust and trustees within 30 days, asking them to explain how they acquired the money or assets. If they fail to respond, other provisions of Chapter 68 apply.
68L.chapter: Chapter VA apply to any person involved in the case of such arrest or seizure, the officer shall make a

68M.title: Certain transfers to be null and voi d
68M.what: If after a certain order or notice, someone transfers any mentioned property, this transfer will be ignored in court proceedings and if the property is later forfeited to the government, it will be considered null and void.
68M.chapter: Chapter VA apply to any person involved in the case of such arrest or seizure, the officer shall make a

68N.title: Cons titution of Appellate Tribunal
68N.what: The Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 12 of the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act, 1976 shall be the Appellate Tribunal for hearing appeals against orders made under sections 68F, 68-I, sub-section (1) of section 68K or section 68L. Any officer referred to in section 68E or any person aggrieved by an order of the competent authority made under these sections may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within forty-five days from the date on which the order is served on them.
68N.chapter: Chapter VA apply to any person involved in the case of such arrest or seizure, the officer shall make a

68P.title: Notice or order not to be in valid for error in description
68P.what: A notice or order issued under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 that contains an error in describing the property or person mentioned will not be considered invalid if the described property or person can still be identified.

68Q.title: Bar of jurisdiction
68Q.what: No order passed or declaration made under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 can be appealed, and no civil court can review matters determined by the Appellate Tribunal or other competent authorities, except as provided in the Act.

68R.title: Competent authority and Appellate Tribunal to have powe rs of civil court
68R.what: The competent authority and the Appellate Tribunal have all powers of a civil court while trying a suit, including summoning people, requiring documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, issuing commissions for witness examination, and other matters as prescribed.

68S.title: Info rmation to competent authority
68S.what: The competent authority can require any government officer or local authority to provide information relevant to the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985.

68T.title: Certain officers to assist Administrator, competent autho rity and Appellate Tribunal
68T.what: Officers who can assist Administrator, competent authority and Appellate Tribunal in proceedings under Chapter.

68U.title: Power to take possession
68U.what: Where property declared forfeited to Central Government or person fails to pay fine, person affected and others in possession must surrender/deliver possession to Administrator within 30 days.

68V.title: Rectification of mistakes
68V.what: If a mistake is found, the authority or tribunal can change an order made within one year of the original date, but they must tell anyone who might be affected and give them a chance to speak.

68W.title: Findings under other laws not conclusive for proceedings under this Chapter
68W.what: No finding made under another law is conclusive in proceedings under this Chapter.

68X.title: Service of notices and orders
68X.what: A notice or order under this Chapter can be served by: (a) giving it to the person, or (b) posting it to their address or attaching it to a place where they were known to have lived or worked.

68Y.title: Punishment for acqui ring property in relation to which proceedings have been taken,
68Y.what: Any person who knowingly acquires property related to an ongoing criminal case under this chapter, faces up to 5 years in prison and a fine of up to ₹50,000.

68Z.title: Release of property in certain cases
68Z.what: Release of property in certain cases where detention order is set aside, a person acquitted or discharged from charges, and appeal is disposed of.

69.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
69.what: No legal action can be taken against the government, its officers, or others if they act in good faith while carrying out their duties under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.

70.title: Central Governm ent and State Government to have regard to international conventions
70.what: The Central Government and State Government must consider international conventions when making rules under this Act, except for other provisions in this Act.

71.title: Power of Government to establish centres for identification, treatment, et c., of addicts and
71.what: The Government may establish or approve as many centres for identification, treatment, management, education, after-care, rehabilitation, social re-integration of addicts, and supply narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances to registered addicts and others where such supply is a medical necessity.

72.title: Recovery of sums due to Government
72.what: The government can deduct or recover a licence fee or other sum due from someone, by attaching and selling their goods or taking it from the person's money.

73.title: Bar of jurisdiction
73.what: No civil court can entertain a suit or proceeding related to: withholding/ cancellation of an opium poppy licence, weighment/examination/classification of opium, or confiscation of adulterated opium.

74.title: Transitional provisions
74.what: Upon the commencement of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985, existing government employees will retain their positions and designations.

74A.title: Power of Central Government to give directions
74A.what: The Central Government may give directions to State Governments on executing Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 provisions.

75.title: Power to delegate
75.what: The Central Government and State Governments can delegate certain powers and functions under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 to specified authorities or officers, subject to conditions and limitations as notified in the Official Gazette.

76.title: Power of Ce ntral Government to make rules
76.what: The Central Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, subject to certain conditions. The rules can cover various matters such as authentication of documents, management of properties, fees for records inspection, powers of civil courts, disposal of confiscated articles, rewards for officers and informers, medical supply conditions, centre establishment and management, committee term and allowances, and any other related matter.

77.title: Rules and notifications to be laid before Parliament
77.what: Every rule made under this Act by the Central Government and every notification or order issued under certain clauses must be laid before Parliament within 30 days, with modifications accepted if both Houses agree.

78.title: Power of State Government to make rules
78.what: The State Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1985 by notifying them in the Official Gazette. The rules can include: providing supplies for medical necessity, establishing and managing centres for addicts, and other related matters.

79.title: Application of the Customs Act, 1962
79.what: The prohibitions and restrictions on import, export, and transit of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances are covered by the Customs Act 1962, with its provisions applying to the mentioned activities. However, if someone is also punishable under both laws, they can be punished under this law instead.

80.title: Application of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 not barred
80.what: The provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 or the rules made thereunder.

81.title: Sa ving of State and special laws
81.what: Nothing in this Act affects the validity of Provincial Acts, State Legislatures' acts, rules with restrictions/punishments not in this Act, or rules with punishments greater than those in this Act for cannabis cultivation/consumption/trafficking.

82.title: Repeal and saving s
82.what: The Opium Act, 1857, the Opium Act, 1878, and the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 are hereby repealed. All actions taken under these laws will continue to be valid as long as they do not conflict with this Act.

83.title: Power to r emove difficulties
83.what: The Central Government can make provisions not inconsistent with this Act to remove difficulties, but such an order must be published in the Official Gazette and made within three years of the Act's assent.

key_points: The court may order confiscation of an article or thing if it determines that the article was used for any purpose other than a permitted one.
Confiscation is not automatic and must be determined by the court on a case-by-case basis.
